newsitem.title: UK: First sugar freight orders emerge citing Iraq.
newsitem.headline: First sugar freight orders emerge citing Iraq.

text.p: Freight orders have started to emerge quoting Iraq as an optional destination for Brazilian bagged sugar cargoes under the United Nations oil-for-food deal, shipbrokers said on Monday. Czarnikow Rionda was looking to cover 14,000 tonnes from south Brazil to Aqaba or Iraq's Gulf port of Umm Qasr for 1/10 January.
Genoc, the shipping arm of French trade house Sucden, quoted for a same-sized cargo from north Brazil to Mediterrean, Red Sea, Umm Qasr, Pakistan or Colombo for prompt/five days notice.

Last week Jordanian traders said Iraq was evaluating more than 120 offers from international sugar houses for supplies of two to four sugar cargoes of between 12,000 and 14,000 tonnes each, with the extent of Iraqi purchases dependent on prices.
Iraq said recently it could import some 300,000 tonnes of sugar over a six-month period when it will be selling oil in exchange for food under a $2 billion deal approved by the U.N.
